judged_text: In addGuests.handler.ts:146-153, EventManager is built with the requester's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. booking.references point at the organizer's credentialIds (the query eagerly loads booking.user.credentials but then doesn't use it), so when the caller is an attendee or team admin, their credential list won't contain the referenced credentialIds — the organizer's real calendar event either silently never gets the new guests or the update throws after guests were already written to the DB.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to call it (attendee or team admin/owner) but then constructs `EventManager` with `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `{...user}` (the caller) rather than the booking organizer. The query eagerly includes `booking.user.credentials` yet those organizer credentials are never used. As a result, when the caller is not the organizer, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` may not have the credential(s) needed to update the organizer’s calendar (especially since booking references are tied to the organizer’s integrations), and this call happens after the DB `attendees.createMany`, risking DB/calendar divergence on failure.
